relevance_note: Cohort study describing three individual male patients with LAMP2 mutations and Danon disease ("Individual clinical details of the three patients with Danon disease are summarized in Table 1").
method_note: Read the paper fully; Table 1 transcribed by hand into a Python build script in scratch, every cell checked against the table and every span verified verbatim by script. Scope: only the 3 LAMP2 patients get rows; the other 7 preexcitation patients (other genes or negative) and the 197-patient LVH cohort are out of scope (cohort_size_as_stated = 197 enrolled; 10 genetically tested). Labels: the text uses lowercase 'patient 1/2/3' most often (Table 1 header uses 'Patient 1/2/3'). Table 1 has patients as columns; the conversion duplicates the 'Patient 1' header column, so in most rows patient 1's value appears twice, while in the serum-enzyme rows (CK, CK-MB, AST, ALT, LDH, cTnT) the row label is repeated into the first data column and patient 1's value is in the second; spans quote the row from its label through the patient's cell. This reading matches the text's fold ranges (e.g. CK 6- to 8-fold, cTnT 14- to 377-fold). Age: Table 1 gives 'Age, years' without saying at what point; recorded as age at diagnosis because the text says 'all were male aged 17–23 years at diagnosis' and Table 2 labels the group mean 'Age at diagnosis'; not recorded as onset or last evaluation. Lab elevations (NT-proBNP, CK, AST, LDH, cTnT) are recorded as observed for each patient from the named-group text ('Laboratory abnormalities were present in all three patients') together with the patient's Table 1 value and normal range. CK-MB and ALT elevations were not recorded per patient: Table 2 gives only counts (1/3, 2/3) without names. Table 1 'Muscle weakness No' (patients 1, 2) excludes muscle weakness only; the checklist item 'proximal muscle weakness (skeletal myopathy)' is left not reported for them (narrower vs composite; patient 1 also had skeletal-muscle LAMP2 absence on biopsy). 'Ventricular fibrillation No' likewise does not exclude the composite 'ventricular tachycardia or fibrillation'. Table 2 zero counts (LVOTO 0, asymmetric hypertrophy 0) exclude no one. LVEF values (61, 62, 45%) are not called reduced or normal by the authors, so the reduced-EF item is not reported. Family history (Table 1: 'Yes (sudden death)', 'Yes (WPW)', 'No') concerns unnamed relatives with no individual-level detail; no relative rows and not recorded as a feature. Variants: nomenclature stated as NM_002294.2 for all three (Figure 2 legend). Patient 2's variant is printed only as 'IVS 1‐2A > G' (no c. notation), so cdna is null. Zygosity and inheritance are not stated; the Limitations say family members were not systematically evaluated. Pathogenicity only recorded for patient 3 ('novel frameshift mutation'). No contradictions found inside the paper. No stacked ' / ' cells.
